name: Thomas G. Jones
role: Deadwood freighter and contractor; partner in Jones & Pennell
bio: T. G. Jones of Deadwood, whose family lived at Billings, was a freighter and contractor and the partner of Joe Pennell in Jones & Pennell. In early 1884 he backed the Medora freight route to the Black Hills. He planned to bring hundreds of horses and mules, traveled the route to Medora in April, and said he would tie himself to the town; the paper later charged that D. T. Bramble induced him to do grading and bridging and then sent his own contracts through Dickinson. From July 1884 into the winter he and Pennell worked a contract on the Canadian Pacific, and in early 1885 he was in New York. In April 1885 he passed through bound for Tacoma, and in November he was in Spearfish with John Guild, backer of the Hay Creek coal road.
